fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is the sole selectable experiment, but no complete product-tagged NAND/COPY matrix, exact factor, target, or legal energy E currently exists. If three independent adverse seam directions survive the omitted rows, the Lean dimension theorem structurally blocks one F_289 leading coordinate; failure of the displayed witness to lift would eliminate only that witness, not prove Q1.

Proposal 2 is killed in its stated form. Bounded toric circuit rank does not imply transfer injectivity: combinations or residue multiples of one or two tagged circuits can still cancel, and projection may recreate Lawrence, diagonal-splice, DROP, and affine-span moves; the proposed support enumeration lacks a fully specified emitted tile and direct below-17E audit.

Proposal 3 is killed for this run. Two coordinates only remove a dimension-three argument if the complete enlarged matrix retains at most four relevant independent directions, while simplex balancing can introduce new kernels and DROP states; no componentwise Q2 propagation or stabilized carry partition is specified.

Proposal 4 is killed absent a fixed-rank recursive gluing construction. Orthogonal module tags detect changes in the pair block, but do not detect internal zero-pair movements, and invertible left/right scalar action does not establish that every parent-child transfer is one bilateral image rather than a canceling sum; no integral positive-definite realization is supplied.

Proposal 5 is killed as formulated. Nonunit Groebner saturation yields at most an algebraic-closure point, not a rational, integral, or finite-residue specialization, while transfer nonvanishing is vector-valued and DROP energy conditions are inequalities; moreover the adverse basis must be recomputed when the emitted architecture changes.

Proposal 6 is killed for the present frontier. Independence of three selected transfers over a larger residue field neither separates the complete projected Graver list nor certifies common energy, DROP, the 17E shell, or Q2, and the required definite order, two-sided prime, graded division structure, and trace threshold are currently unverified.

Proposal 7 is killed as a frontier experiment. A generic certificate checker supplies no new mechanism, its proposed NAND-first instantiation repeats an already verified local survivor, and assumptions such as exhaustive adverse shells and nonzero transfers largely contain Q1; Graver-term nonvanishing alone is also invalid because transfers can cancel in conformal sums.
evidence: The verified 4x2 seam has a conformally primitive zero-margin, zero-product-tag movement of squared coefficient weight 8, and the independent 8x8 stress test has a zero-transfer two-rectangle movement of weight 12. Neither is yet a full-tile or CVP-energy witness.

Lean verifies both rectangle factorization/nonvanishing and that every three F_289 symbols, viewed as F_17^2, have a nontrivial residue dependency. These are local algebraic facts, not Q1 or lift certificates.

The supplied verifier evidence contains no complete emitted product-tagged NAND/COPY matrix, common legal energy, DROP bound, full adverse shell, or P-adic carry table. Therefore no proposal currently proves Q1, Q2, amplification, or an asymptotic gap.

ROADMAP and both Generation-3 gate reviews identify the same next discriminator: lift the certified rectangle dependency through every row of the actual matrices and optimize its exact energy. Proposal 1 directly performs that bounded frontier test; the other proposals mutate the architecture or build proof infrastructure before resolving it.
next_experiment: Select Proposal 1 only. Hash-lock the actual N=8 product-tagged NAND/fusion matrix and both COPY orientations, emitting every anchor, normalization, legality, calibration, port, glue, pair-selector, and transfer coordinate plus the exact target and legal energy E; use SNF to test whether each sign of the certified 4x2 dependency extends through all non-transfer rows, and for every extension exactly minimize the full positive-definite objective over the remaining integral coordinates below 17E. A sub-17E adverse extension kills the single-coordinate candidate; no extension only clears this dependency and must stop without claiming Q1 or adding Graver, multiple-tag, or P^3 work.
